settings.subtitle: A family record from Aalesund to Pike Lake
settings.summary: The Calders came from the coast of Norway to the ore docks of Duluth in 1900. This is their record: Ruth Calder's recordings, Henrik's letters from France, the manifest of the ship Anders crossed on, the ore dock's payroll, and the cabin on Pike Lake.

chapter_templates.name: Ancestor chapter
chapter_templates.blurb: One relative per chapter. Says what kind of story it is, carries a line of descent, ends with THE RECORDS.
sections: Opening: what kind of story this is

chapter_templates.name: Life stage
chapter_templates.blurb: Childhood, college, the move west. Stories in order, joined by narration, opening on a concrete moment.

chapter_templates.name: Theme across a life
chapter_templates.blurb: One thread — a trade, a faith, a friendship, a place — followed across decades.

chapter_templates.name: Photo album
chapter_templates.blurb: Photographs with evidence-coded captions and little text.

narrative_styles.name: Biographer
narrative_styles.blurb: Third person, past tense, written about them. Their words quoted exactly. The house style.

narrative_styles.name: As told to
narrative_styles.blurb: First person, in their voice, lightly edited. Reads like them talking.

narrative_styles.name: Documentary
narrative_styles.blurb: Third person, spare and factual, records foregrounded. Good for research-heavy chapters.

narrative_styles.name: Letter to the grandchildren
narrative_styles.blurb: Addressed to the family who will read it. Warmest; use sparingly.

voice_samples.biographer: When she was seven or eight, as best she remembered, Ruth walked her father's lunch down to the ore dock in a tin pail. The dock was so tall "you had to tip your head all the way back," and the trains ran right out on top of it. Whether it frightened her, she never quite settled: "No. Well, yeah. A little."
voice_samples.as-told-to: When I was little, maybe seven or eight, I'd walk my dad's lunch down to the ore dock. A tin pail. And the dock was so tall you had to tip your head all the way back. Was I scared of it? No. Well, yeah. A little.
voice_samples.documentary: Around 1945 (she gave her age as "maybe seven or eight"), Ruth carried her father's lunch to the Duluth ore dock. She described the structure as so tall "you had to tip your head all the way back," with trains running along its top. No photograph of the visit is known.
voice_samples.letter: You never saw the ore dock, and I only saw it with my head tipped all the way back. I carried your great-great-grandfather's lunch down to it in a tin pail when I was seven or eight. Was I scared? A little. I'll admit that much now.

photo_styles.name: Tintype
photo_styles.blurb: 1850s–70s. Plate edges, shallow focus, slight silver bloom.

photo_styles.name: Silver gelatin
photo_styles.blurb: 1890s–1940s. Grey scale, fine grain, studio lighting.

photo_styles.name: Pen and ink
photo_styles.blurb: Drawn, not photographic. Never mistaken for a record.

quick_prompts.label: Who are the relatives in my sources?
quick_prompts.prompt: Read every source in this project (transcripts in transcript/clean/ and anything in sources/). List every relative who is named or described: their name as said, how they relate to the subject, the timestamps where they come up, and whether each relationship is witnessed, told to the subject, or family lore. Flag spellings you are unsure of. Don't search the web yet.

quick_prompts.label: Search the public records for the oldest ancestor
quick_prompts.prompt: Find the oldest ancestor named in the sources. Using the records-archives skill, search free public sources (census, military rosters, ship registers, newspapers, grave records, museum catalogues) for that person. For each hit give the record, where it lives, a link, and whether it corroborates or contradicts the family's version. Cache what you find under facts/records/. Never send my personal details to any site.

quick_prompts.label: Propose a chapter map
quick_prompts.prompt: Using the chapter-index-builder skill, propose a chapter map for this book from the story units and the timeline: a family-history part and a life part, each chapter with title, years, the units it uses and a one-line summary. Write it to data/chapters.csv with status proposed and stop for my approval. Batch any questions.

quick_prompts.label: Draft a preview of chapter 1
quick_prompts.prompt: Draft chapter 1 as a preview, following the memoir-style-guide skill exactly: third person, quotes exact from the transcript, every paragraph cited with // src:, anything you add as a #bridge. Build the draft PDF and tell me where it is and what you flagged for review.

quick_prompts.label: What's still unapproved?
quick_prompts.prompt: List everything still waiting on me: unapproved bridges, // REVIEW: notes, open gates (speaker confirmation, chapter map, final sign-off) and the questions in facts/gaps.md. Group them by chapter and give file and line for each.
